question: Can the Engineering team use GitHub Copilot?
expected_citation_text: GitHub Copilot — Engineering team only.
notes: Direct lookup. Explicitly listed in approved tools table.

question: Can a Marketing team member use GitHub Copilot for writing ad copy?
expected_citation_text: Engineering team only.
notes: Direct lookup. Copilot is Engineering-only, Marketing is excluded.

question: Is it allowed to record a meeting with a client using Otter.ai?
expected_citation_text: Internal meetings only. No client calls without consent.
notes: Direct lookup. Otter.ai restriction is explicit.

question: Can any employee use Claude for writing assistance?
expected_citation_text: All teams. No confidential data without encryption.
notes: Direct lookup. Claude approved for all teams.

question: Can an employee input customer names and emails into Claude?
expected_citation_text: Inputting personally identifiable information (PII) of customers into any AI tool not certified for PII handling.
notes: Direct lookup. Names and emails are PII, prohibited explicitly.

question: Can an employee use AI to make a final hiring decision?
expected_citation_text: Using AI to make final decisions on hiring, firing, performance reviews.
notes: Direct lookup. AI assist is allowed but not final decision.

question: Can an employee use a personal ChatGPT subscription for internal company work?
expected_citation_text: Using personal AI subscriptions (not company-provisioned) for company work involving any data classified as Internal, Confidential, or Restricted.
notes: Direct lookup. Personal subscriptions prohibited for company work.

question: Does TechNova monitor employee AI tool usage on company devices?
expected_citation_text: TechNova IT may monitor AI tool usage on company devices and company-provisioned accounts.
notes: Factual lookup. Answer is yes, monitoring is permitted.

question: Can an employee use Grammarly to proofread a Restricted document?
expected_citation_text: Grammarly — No restricted documents.
notes: Direct lookup. Grammarly has explicit restriction on restricted docs.

question: How long does an approved policy exception last?
expected_citation_text: Approved exceptions are logged in the IT Security exception registry and expire after 90 days.
notes: Factual lookup. 90-day expiry is explicit.

question: Can a contractor use Claude to summarize an Internal TechNova document?
expected_citation_section: Section 2 — Approved AI Tools, Section 5 — Contractor and Vendor Rules
expected_citation_text: Claude approved for all teams. Contractors must follow same rules as full-time employees.
notes: Inference required. Contractor + Internal data + approved tool. All three must be checked.

question: Can a contractor use Claude to work with a client's data if their manager verbally said it was fine?
expected_citation_text: Verbal approval from a TechNova manager does not constitute policy authorization for contractors. Written confirmation is required for every exception.
notes: Inference required. Verbal approval is explicitly insufficient for contractors.

question: Can an HR employee use Claude to draft a performance review document?
expected_citation_section: Section 2 — Approved AI Tools, Section 3 — Prohibited Uses
expected_citation_text: Claude approved for all teams. AI may assist with drafting, not deciding.
notes: Inference required. Drafting is allowed; final decision cannot be AI-made.

question: A sales employee wants to use a new AI prospecting tool not on the approved list. Can they try it out to evaluate it?
expected_citation_text: Unapproved tools may not be used even on a trial basis.
notes: Inference required. Trial use is explicitly covered and prohibited.

question: An employee publishes a blog post that was 40% written by Claude without disclosure. Is this a violation?
expected_citation_text: Any client-facing document where more than 30% of the content was generated by an AI tool must be disclosed.
notes: Inference required. 40% exceeds the 30% threshold, disclosure was required.

question: Can an engineer use Claude to help write code that will go into production?
expected_citation_section: Section 2 — Approved AI Tools, Section 7 — AI-Generated Content and Disclosure
expected_citation_text: Claude approved for all teams. Code submitted for production deployment where AI generated more than 50% of the logic requires disclosure.
notes: Inference required. Allowed but disclosure rule applies if >50% AI-generated.

question: Can an employee use Claude with a Confidential document if their manager approves per use?
expected_citation_section: Section 4 — Data Classification and AI Use
expected_citation_text: Confidential: Only tools with signed DPA. Requires manager approval per use.
notes: Inference required. Manager approval per use is explicitly required.

question: An employee used an unapproved tool urgently to meet a client deadline, then got it approved afterward. Is this okay?
expected_citation_text: Exceptions are not retroactive. Using a tool before an exception is approved is a policy violation even if the exception is later granted.
notes: Inference required. Retroactive exception explicitly doesn't protect prior use.

question: Can an employee use Otter.ai to transcribe a meeting with a client if the client has given verbal consent?
expected_citation_text: No client calls without consent.
notes: Inference required. Policy says 'without consent' — verbal consent exists but policy doesn't specify written. Escalation recommended.

question: Can an employee share unpublished acquisition target information with Claude to draft a summary for their manager?
expected_citation_text: Sharing unpublished financial data, acquisition targets, or M&A activity with any AI tool, approved or not.
notes: Inference required. The prohibition applies even to approved tools.

question: A contractor has a personal Claude subscription and is using it for TechNova work on publicly available data. Is this allowed?
expected_citation_section: Section 3 — Prohibited Uses, Section 5 — Contractor and Vendor Rules
expected_citation_text: Personal AI subscriptions prohibited for Internal, Confidential, or Restricted data. Contractors must disclose all AI tools used.
notes: Edge case. Public data + personal subscription — prohibition only covers Internal/Confidential/Restricted. But disclosure rule still applies. Escalation recommended.

question: An employee's manager verbally told them they could use a new unapproved AI tool. Can they use it?
expected_citation_section: Section 2 — Approved AI Tools, Section 6 — Escalation and Exceptions
expected_citation_text: Unapproved tools may not be used even on a trial basis. Written approval from manager AND IT Security review required.
notes: Edge case. Verbal manager approval is not sufficient — written + IT Security required.

question: Can an employee use an approved AI tool on a document they are unsure how to classify?
expected_citation_section: Section 4 — Data Classification and AI Use
expected_citation_text: When in doubt about a document's classification, treat it as Confidential.
notes: Edge case. Policy instructs treating unknown as Confidential — which requires manager approval per use.

question: An employee used Claude to write 25% of an internal report and didn't disclose it. Is this a violation?
expected_citation_text: Any internal document submitted as original research or analysis must disclose AI assistance.
notes: Edge case. Threshold (30%) not crossed for client-facing, but 'internal document submitted as original research' has its own disclosure rule without a percentage threshold.

question: A contractor urgently needs to process Restricted data with an AI tool for a TechNova project. Can their TechNova contact approve this verbally?
expected_citation_section: Section 4 — Data Classification and AI Use, Section 5 — Contractor and Vendor Rules
expected_citation_text: Restricted data: No AI tools without CISO written approval. Verbal approval not sufficient for contractors.
notes: Edge case. Multiple stacked restrictions: Restricted data requires CISO written approval, contractor verbal rule, urgency explicitly not grounds for bypassing.

question: Can an employee report a colleague's suspected AI policy violation anonymously?
expected_citation_text: Employees are encouraged to report suspected violations by colleagues to the IT Security team anonymously via the internal ethics hotline.
notes: Factual edge case. Direct answer exists but most employees wouldn't know to look here.

question: An employee's exception was approved 85 days ago. Can they continue using the tool for another 30 days?
expected_citation_text: Approved exceptions expire after 90 days.
notes: Edge case. 85+30=115 days — exceeds 90-day limit. They need to reapply before day 90.

question: Can an employee use AI to assist in drafting a termination letter if a manager reviews and approves it?
expected_citation_text: AI may assist with drafting, not deciding. Using AI to make final decisions on firing is prohibited.
notes: Edge case. Drafting with human review/approval is the key distinction from prohibited final decision-making.
